    # Per demo, color stretches of background from each boundary marker to any
    # interior marker position, leaving the marker color at boundaries intact.
    g=[row[:] for row in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    border=next((g[r][0] for r in range(h) if g[r][0]!=g[0][1]), None)
    bg=g[0][1]
    accent=next((v for row in g for v in row if v not in (bg,border)),None)
    if accent is None: return g
    # One side border occupies the contiguous non-bg run on the corresponding edge.
    top=[]
    for c in range(w):
        if all(g[r][c]==border for r in range( min(6,h))): top.append(c)
    left=[]
    for r in range(h):
        if g[r][0]==border: left.append(r)
    # Determine color fill direction from boundary segments and marker.
    # Fill each horizontal region's interior cells through marker column,
    # and vertical regions through marker row.
    # Demo indicates only rows/cols containing border-segment continuity are
    # patterned using marker color, with marker at the endpoint as separator.
    for r,row in enumerate(g):
        positions=[c for c,v in enumerate(row) if v==accent]
        if positions:
            c=positions[0]
            for x in range(1,c): g[r][x]=1
            g[r][c]=4
    # For border on top/bottom, fill row sections whose vertical boundary is marker.
    # General: boundary colored strip indicates active span, fill on that strip's
    # orthogonal direction up to encountered marker-derived coordinate.
    if left:
        for r in left:
            # marker targets in row give length
            ps=[c for c,v in enumerate(g[r]) if v==accent]
            if ps:
                for c in range(1,ps[0]): g[r][c]=1
                g[r][ps[0]]=4

if __name__=='__main__':

        elif any(grid[0][x]==border for x in range(w)):

            g[r][c]=4

",
